PullRequest.Title: agentHost: move never-run nested sessions and sessions not yet loaded
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. -->

Fixes two ways a nested session could not be moved with the Move Chats feature (behind `chat.agentHost.moveChats.enabled`, default off).

**F4: a never-run peer chat could not be moved.** A peer chat created by "New Nested Session" that never ran a turn has a legacy `session_chats.is_read` of NULL (peer creation writes no read state), while the verified per-chat aggregate says `isRead: true` (new chats are created idle and read). The catalog normalizer compared them strictly and refused the move with `sessionNotReady` ("Legacy peer state differs from verified per-chat source"). A NULL legacy `is_read` now reads as read; a real divergence (aggregate says unread) is still refused.

**Sessions the host has not loaded could not be nested.** The host publishes `vscode.movable` only for sessions it has loaded, so after a restart a single-chat session reported `canMoveSessionUnder=false` until opened, and `moveSession` did not restore its source (only `moveChat` restored its target). Design is "load at move time":
- Client (`canMoveSessionUnder`): offers the nest for any unarchived single-chat session when the host supports `vscode.sessionMove`, from list data alone. It no longer reads `vscode.movable` (which can only be `true` or absent, so it cannot say "not movable"); no loading, no per-row subscriptions.
- Host: `moveSession` (and the AHP `moveChat` source) restores an unloaded session inside the move sequencer via the existing `restoreSession`, then runs the normal checks, so the usual `AgentChatMoveRefusedError` reaches the user. A session that can't be restored is refused (`notMovable` / `sessionNotReady`) with nothing changed. Host publishing of `vscode.movable` is unchanged.

## How to test
Unit tests (all passing together, 1820 tests):
- `scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentService.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostDatabase.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts` → 1820 passing
- `npm run eslint -- <changed .ts files>` → clean
- `npm run typecheck-client` → clean (no errors)
- Hygiene ran in the pre-commit hook → passed

Not run: Azure pipeline 111 e2e at the time of writing (queued after PR creation).

Scenarios.Scenario: Evaluating whether a session-list row can be nested under another session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The provider resolves the cached adapter and synchronously reads connection capability, archived state, and the cached chat-array length. No asynchronous work or boundary must complete.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One constant-time lookup per eligibility query; even if queried across a session list, cost scales linearly with visible rows and performs no per-row I/O.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous local reads only; no queue, IPC, filesystem, database, or network concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Uses already-hydrated _sessionCache data. Cold sessions are not loaded and no negative-cache retry is created; warm behavior is the same constant-time observable read.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed method and repository-wide callers show only Map/observable reads, and the test explicitly checks that answering eligibility adds no wire operations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The generic UI may query eligibility at different frequencies, but each query is bounded O(1) local work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The diff replaces one constant-time metadata read with two constant-time cached observable reads and does not add subscriptions, allocations proportional to chat count, or boundary calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: Moving a single-chat session whose source has not been loaded since host restart
Scenarios.CriticalPath: One existing renderer-to-host moveSession request enters the global chat-move sequencer. The newly added source restore must finish, then the existing destination restore/catalog preparation/database validation and move commit complete before the user-visible move returns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send vscode/moveSession over the existing extension request/data plane.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same IPC request was sent, but an unloaded source was refused by the host before a successful move path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The request/response brackets the whole move and is on the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read registry, catalog, session metadata, chat state, and annotations while restoring the source.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced restore for the cold source; fixed per-session database reads, with existing per-chat hydration inside restore.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The unloaded source was not restored and the operation returned NotMovable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Newly required before an unloaded source can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve provider chat metadata/backing and materialize the restored source; on a metadata miss the provider catalog may be enumerated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per cold source restore; full provider-catalog enumeration only on the existing cold metadata-miss path and shared provider initialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No source provider restoration occurred because the move was refused.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the explicit move when source state is cold.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore the destination if cold, prepare both catalogs, read their revision snapshots, and commit the move.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one destination restore plus fixed grouped reads for the source/target pair per move.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Destination restoration and grouped catalog work already occurred once a move reached this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing critical-path work for a successful move.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Exactly one source and one destination per explicit drag/drop. The added work is one source-session restore on a cold source; it does not scale with the number of rows. A provider metadata miss can trigger the existing provider-catalog enumeration, whose cost scales with that provider's catalog size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All chat/session moves are serialized by _chatMoveSequencer. Restore work is coalesced per session by _restoreSessionInFlight, and resident sessions bypass restoration. Session residency is bounded by the default limit of 10 and reconciliation/eviction.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm source and target states skip restore. Concurrent restores of the same cold session join one promise. Successful restores become resident but are governed by AgentSessionResidency; failed metadata lookup may warm the existing provider catalog rather than repeating independent work per row.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added await is directly on the explicit move path, and restore's database/provider boundaries, per-session coalescing, resident fast path, global move sequencer, and residency cap are all explicit in code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold provider restore duration varies; a large legacy provider catalog can be slow on a metadata miss. The feature is default-off and the path is one explicit move, not list rendering or startup.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The extra cold restore is the bounded work required to turn a previously immediate refusal into a successful operation; it is deferred until move time, coalesced, cached by residency, and does not fan out by session-list size.

Scenarios.Scenario: Moving a chat whose source session is not resident
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The explicit moveChat request enters the same global sequencer. For a session destination, the newly added source restore completes before existing validation, target restore, catalog snapshot reads, folder/worktree preparation, and commit. Promotion to a new session returns before the new restore call and is unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Hydrate source registry/catalog/session state before validating and moving its chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced restore for one cold source per explicit move.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The move validation read absent state and refused; it did not hydrate the source.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Added to the critical path only when the source is not resident.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Provider metadata lookup/materialization during cold source restore.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider lookup/materialization for the cold source, with existing catalog fallback on a miss.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No source provider restore occurred on this previously refused path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing target restore, grouped catalog snapshot reads, and move persistence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One target and one grouped source/target operation per move, plus existing moved-subtree persistence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Already performed for successful moves with resident sources.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One source restore per cold source session and at most one target restore per explicit move; existing subtree/folder work scales with the moved chat subtree, not with all listed sessions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Globally serialized moves; per-session restore coalescing prevents duplicate concurrent source hydration. No new parallel burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Resident sources skip the added restore. Cold successful restores are retained within the bounded residency cache; in-flight restores are joined. Promotion-to-new-session does not invoke the new source restore branch.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: branch placement proves new-session promotion is unaffected and cold session-destination moves add exactly one guarded source restore.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The UI prevalence of stale/unloaded source requests and provider restore duration are not measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. This is deferred, bounded first-use work that enables a previously unsupported cold-source operation, with no per-row or per-chat fan-out beyond existing restore semantics.

Scenarios.Scenario: Normalizing a legacy chat catalog where a peer has no recorded read state
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing catalog-normalization transaction performs its existing session_chats SELECT and per-chat validation. The changed expression only treats null is_read as read during an in-memory scalar comparison.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read legacy session_chats and write/apply the normalized catalog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing grouped SELECT for the session plus existing normalization writes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same query and normalization pass ran, but null versus aggregate-read caused a conflict.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing reconciliation/normalization path; the changed null comparison adds no boundary operation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Existing normalization remains linear in the session's chat count. The diff adds no loop, query, allocation proportional to input, or serialization.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unchanged database transaction/sequencing; no new concurrency or boundary burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache behavior changes; the same already-read legacy row and aggregate chat objects are compared.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete changed hunk is a null-coalescing/scalar comparison inside the existing per-chat normalization function.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Session chat counts vary, but the asymptotic and boundary behavior are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; the change only alters comparison semantics in already-executed work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all eight changed files and traced eligibility, move-time restoration, protocol dispatch, provider/session restoration, catalog normalization, restore coalescing, global move serialization, and residency eviction. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance issue was found, and the PR does not itself establish a shipped performance-regression fix requiring blame.
